students are expected to use AI transparently and responsibly.
AI may support differentiation, feedback, and access, but must not replace human relationships, professional judgment, or essential skill development.
AI systems must be monitored for bias and disparate impact.
Access to AIsupported learning must not widen opportunity gaps.
AI integration must comply with FERPA, COPPA, PPRA, IDEA, ADA, Section 504, COMAR, and applicable Maryland law.
Districts must enforce data minimization, contractual safeguards, and cybersecurity protections.

Schools must clearly define appropriate AI use, require transparency when AI is permitted, and redesign assessments to emphasize reasoning, process, and authentic demonstration of learning rather than reliance on detection tools.
Rolespecific professional learning must equip teachers, leaders, and staff to evaluate AI outputs critically and use tools responsibly.
Students must develop the knowledge and skills to understand how AI systems function, evaluate bias and limitations, protect privacy, and use AI ethically across disciplines and grade levels.
High-stakes operational systems, including predictive analytics and automated decision-support tools, require documented human review, equity monitoring, and transparent communication.

Districts must apply structured evaluation criteria, contractual protections, and ongoing monitoring to ensure that AI tools meet standards for privacy, accessibility, transparency, and instructional value.

payload.text: AACPS complies with federal, State, and local laws that prohibit discrimination based on membership of a protected class.

The Board prohibits:

a. Discrimination in its educational programs and in employment on the basis of actual or perceived race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, sexual orientation, genetic information, gender identity, gender expression, disability, homeless status, or military status;

In accordance with the law and its commitments, the Board prohibits the use of language and the display of symbols that promote hate, demean an identifiable person or group of persons, or are reasonably perceived as promoting hatred, bullying, cyberbullying, harassment, or intimidation, and can be reasonably forecasted to cause substantial disruption to the orderly operation of a school or AACPS operations or activities.

The use or display of a symbol of hate on AACPS property, on a school bus or other school vehicle, at school-sponsored activities, or in any manner that substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a school regardless of where the incident occurs is prohibited and may be considered a hate crime under federal or State law.

Complaints of unlawful discrimination shall be promptly and appropriately investigated in accordance with Policy GAGG and Regulation GAGG-RA - Nondiscrimination and Anti-Harassment - Personnel as well as Policy JO and Regulation JO-RA - Bias Behavior and Language.
payload.mechanism_stated: in accordance with Policy GAGG and Regulation GAGG-RA - Nondiscrimination and Anti-Harassment - Personnel as well as Policy JO and Regulation JO-RA - Bias Behavior and Language

payload.text: Data Owner - an individual who has the requisite knowledge, administrative control, and has been officially designated as accountable for specific data elements or data sets.
Data Steward - an individual who is responsible for maintaining data quality and security.
Education Records - those records that are directly related to a student and maintained by AACPS or by a party acting for AACPS.
Personally Identifiable Information - information that, alone or in combination, makes it possible to identify an individual student with reasonable certainty.
